## A) Agenda answers

**Q1 — λ.** Keep fixed λ = 1. Nested CV-selected λ is unreliable with only 9–13 episode blocks; it picks λ = 30–100 in early windows, loses 9.4 pp in 1970s–80s origins, and the nested-minus-fixed difference (−8.7 pp, SD 5.5) is not beyond 1.96 SD but is clearly worse. Switching now would be post hoc. Headline from 2027: operational = fixed-λ curve-only +27.05 % on 198 origins; every skill statement prints the triplet fixed-λ / nested (+18.32 %) / oracle-free (+20.37 %), with fixed-λ first. Do not make nested the headline.

**Q2 — Model selection and the gate.** Amend §4 formally: curve-only is operational by council decision, not by per-origin selection; no selector runs at refit. The F5 benchmark gate is two-tier and never automatic: |Δ| > 4.42 pp Triggers next council agenda; |Δ| > 21.06 pp (own block MDE) is treated as evidence only if the advantage is not carried by one block and is robust to universe start. E1 shows every non-degenerate selector loses 9–10 pp and F5’s inner advantage is 72–76 % one-block; E3 shows F5 is start-sensitive. This amends D2.

**Q3 — Frequency.** Keep quarterly fit. Monthly full-curve +29.24 % is only +2.19 pp above quarterly +27.05 %, below the v5.0.1 block-MDE 2.99, and monthly evaluation uses 591 overlapping 12-month origins. The live input is already monthly, so §2’s timeliness argument is met. Record G1.3 as “literal reading passes, code reading fails 26.03 vs 26.05; status quo retained due to overlap inflation”; publish monthly as permanent supplement.

**Q4 — Universe start.** Keep 1947Q2. Moving to 1953Q2/1960Q1 would lower current P by 2.5/4.5 pp after seeing that effect; common-origin skill differences (+20.5 vs +21.4/+21.9) are small. The Shiller LTR proxy is a documented caveat, not a disqualifier. Print the start-sensitivity line (14.9/12.4/10.4 at live curve) in every fit report.

**Q5 — Demotion.** Document that the five incumbents survive only under the asymmetric v5.1 rule; under a symmetric bar, nobody is demoted, and neutral LL gives curve+cape +29.69 but fails pre-1990 and is below MDE 4.42. No operational demotion now. For F5, label it “legacy benchmark, not a validated alternative.” For any future search, require one symmetric add/drop bar (≥ +2/+2 pp, ≥7/8 folds, sign stable) fixed in sealed spec, plus leave-one-block-out diagnostics against the 1947–48 single-block trap.

**Q6 — Content trigger.** Adopt it from 2027. It is mechanical, removes a 0–9 month lag depending on NBER trough announcements, costs 18 net extra refits in 49 years, and max |ΔP| is 1.05 pp. Post hoc but acceptable: deterministic, no thresholds relaxed. Content-triggered refits must be full refits under the same preregistration and no feature search.

**Q7 — Ledger key.** Do not amend the key. E5 shows the logged base-rate rule is generous (22.8 % vs realized 15.3 %), but changing it after row 4 would corrupt the ledger. Publish E5 as a supplement with all three censoring variants (+24.41 / +28.95 / +33.28) and ex-post pooled base rate +21.2. State publicly: cluster-t reaches 80 % power only at ≈150 calendar years; ≈18 years only if the invalid 2020–24 block is excluded; naive iid tests reject 36–53 % at 5–20 years; parametric 112–183 years. The ledger is an honesty instrument, not a powered test.

**Q8 — EBP/Baa.** Defer. No sealed test before 2027: EBP onset values already seen, revision risk unaudited, Baa-10y not redistributable, and power too low (MDE ≈4.4 pp with only ~3 EBP onsets before 1990). Re-examine only after ≥12 monthly EBP snapshots show no material revision. Baa-10y stays closed unless a redistributable source is secured.

**Q9 — L_R.** Peak-only. The label is onset; a positive origin matures when the peak announcement identifies the onset, independent of trough announcements. Including trough announcements would lift L_R to 21 and change eligible origins unjustifiably. Fix the code before the audit runs; document L_R = 18 = floor as peak-announcement lag.

**Q10 — Ratification.** Ratify all four individually: (i) trailing-month daily DGS10−DTB3, with monthly GS10−TB3MS permanently printed on every row; (ii) tripwires moved out of the ignition column, documented as restoring R3; (iii) log day = first weekday from the 10th +3 days; (iv) live censoring inside an announced recession. Each must appear in the manifest with effective date and no retroactive edits.

## B) Verdict on Claude’s draft positions

- **Keep as written:** D1, D4, D5, D6, D8, D9, D10.
- **Amend D2:** add the numeric own MDE 21.06 pp and require one-block/start-robustness before F5 evidence.
- **Amend D3:** retain quarterly fit, but replace the “tie” rationale with the overlap-inflation and below-MDE rationale; publish monthly as a permanent supplement.
- **Amend D7:** state the power figures explicitly (≈150 years; 18 only under an invalid exclusion; 36–53 % naive over-rejection; 112–183 parametric) and attach them to LOG.md.
- **Strike:** none.

## C) Biggest risk

The biggest risk is that keeping λ = 1, quarterly fit, and 1947Q2 simultaneously preserves the combination that gives the highest published skill (+27.05 %) and current P ≈14.8 %, after seeing alternatives. If the 2027 refit declines toward ≈+21 % and another 2020–24-style false alarm occurs, this will look like post hoc status-quo selection. Mitigation: preregister the fixed-λ/nested/oracle-free triplet, state all three as protocol constants chosen under post hoc scrutiny, and never claim they were a priori.
